name: FPGA
definition: A chip of programmable logic blocks and wires onto which a digital design is loaded~\cite{jamiesonthesis}.

name: flip-flop
definition: A one-bit storage cell that keeps its value between clock edges~\cite{jamiesonthesis}.

name: LUT
definition: Look-up table: a small memory that implements any logic function of $K$ inputs ($K=6$ here). A LUT and a flip-flop form the basic logic element of most FPGAs~\cite{jamiesonthesis}.

name: CLB
definition: Configurable logic block: a group of LUTs and flip-flops that is placed as one unit (a cluster in~\cite{jamiesonthesis})~\cite{luuthesis}.

name: Verilog / HDL
definition: The hardware description language (HDL) in which a designer writes a circuit; Verilog is the one used here~\cite{jamiesonthesis}.

name: netlist
definition: The list of the gates, LUTs and other cells of a design and the wires (nets) between them~\cite{jamiesonthesis}.

name: synthesis front end
definition: The program that reads the HDL and produces a netlist for the rest of the flow~\cite{jamiesonthesis}.

name: elaboration
definition: The first step of a front end: turn the parsed HDL into a design graph by resolving parameters, generate loops and hierarchy~\cite{jamiesonthesis}.

name: ABC
definition: ABC is a public-domain system for logic synthesis of binary logic circuits; its technology mapping matches the logic of a netlist with LUTs~\cite{brayton2010abc}.

name: packing, placement, routing
definition: Packing groups LUTs and flip-flops into CLBs; placement chooses a site on the chip for each CLB; routing chooses the wires between them~\cite{jamiesonthesis}.

name: VTR / VPR
definition: The open-source FPGA CAD flow (Verilog-to-Routing, VTR) and its packing, placement and routing program (VPR)~\cite{luuthesis}.

name: Odin II / Yosys / Parmys
definition: Odin II was the front end of VTR; Yosys is an open synthesis tool and Parmys the Yosys plugin that now serves VTR as its front end.

name: provenance
definition: The link from each netlist object back to the HDL that produced it.

name: Dark Factory
definition: A software process in which agents turn a human's specification into software, with no human writing the code.

name: channel width
definition: The number of routing tracks in each channel that the router needs to route a design (minimum channel width $W$)~\cite{luuthesis}.

name: wirelength
definition: The total length of the wires a routed design uses.

name: critical path / CPD
definition: The slowest path between registers and its delay in ns (critical-path delay, CPD)~\cite{luuthesis}.

name: near-critical
definition: A path whose delay is within a stated window of the critical-path delay.

name: area
definition: How much chip a design uses: the number of LUTs, the number of CLBs and the minimum channel width $W$.

name: speed
definition: How fast the circuit runs: the critical-path delay and the routed wirelength, and where available the near-critical paths.

name: power
definition: The energy the circuit uses. This paper does not measure it.

name: hypothesis / verdict
definition: A hypothesis is a claim that an experiment can confirm or fail to confirm. The verdict is USEFUL (confirmed under the stated gate or check), POSSIBLY GOOD (confirmed but narrow or fragile), INCONCLUSIVE (neither confirmed nor failed) or DISMISSED (failed).

name: IR
definition: Intermediate representation: Odin III's one internal design graph, with a view of multi-bit words and a view of single bits.

name: oracle
definition: A trusted reference tool whose output we compare against. Here the oracles are the forest of Yosys with Parmys, Odin II, ABC and VTR's stored results.

name: C ABI / plugin
definition: The application binary interface (ABI) is the stable C interface through which a plugin, a separately built program that adds passes or cell types, and AI tools drive Odin III without changing it.

name: AST
definition: Abstract syntax tree: the parsed form of the HDL text, a tree of the declarations, statements and expressions with their source locations.

name: golden
definition: The stored result of an oracle for a design, kept so that later runs compare against it.

name: partial mapping
definition: Binding the parts of a design that fit the architecture's dedicated blocks (multipliers, adders, memories) to those blocks and leaving the rest as gates for ABC~\cite{jamiesonthesis}.

name: word cell / bit cell / lower
definition: A word cell is a multi-bit operator in the IR; a bit cell is a one-bit gate; the pass lower turns word cells into bit cells.

name: proc, opt, fsm, wreduce, flatten
definition: The word-level passes re-implemented from Yosys 0.55: processes to multiplexers and flip-flops; clean-up; state-machine recoding; width reduction; inlining of the hierarchy.

name: BLIF
definition: The netlist text format that VPR reads.

name: lineage DAG
definition: The append-only graph of source, imported and derived records, with labelled joins, that sits behind each provenance ID.

name: geomean ratio
definition: The geometric mean over designs of the ratio Odin III over Parmys; 1.0 means equal and below 1.0 is better for area and delay.

name: leg (P, O, O$'$)
definition: One run of the quality-of-results harness: P is the Parmys flow (the baseline), O is Odin III with its linked ABC, and O$'$ is Odin III's netlist through VTR's own ABC stage.

name: QoR gate
definition: The acceptance bound on quality of results: geomean ratio at most 1.20 and no design above 1.50 on the gated metrics.
search: QoR gate|1\.20 gate|gate of 1\.20|1\.20 and no

name: equivalence (SAT, refinement)
definition: A proof, by SAT, that two designs give the same outputs, or that one refines the other; unproven when the design is past the size limit of the solver.

name: fcheck (functional check)
definition: VTR's random check: build the RTL and the netlist with Verilator and drive both with 50,000 random vectors.

name: determinism
definition: Rerunning gives byte-identical output.

name: exit-code discipline
definition: A list of expected differences never turns an unproven result into a pass; tools report 0 holds, 1 differs, 2 tool error, 3 hard failure, 4 unproven, 77 skipped.
